questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Turkmenistan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Climate” part of the Turkmenistan article.

questions.proof: The highest temperature recorded in Ashgabat is 48.0 °C (118.4 °F).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Turkmenistan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Turkmenistan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Turkmenistan article.

questions.proof: It has borders with Afghanistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Turkmenistan about 491,210 square kilometres; Oman about 309,500 square kilometres; Bulgaria about 110,994 square kilometres; United Arab Emirates about 83,600 square kilometres.
